so all fanbord configs for ventura probe on FruDevice interface, it should always have the `$bus` property, right?

Do you think there is another bug here besides the trailing `$` thing.

I don't think the math calculating logic in templateCharReplace supports more than one variable in a JSON value string. But there's a logic in perform_scan that has supported the maths in the ventura fan board config until `handleLeftOverTemplateVars` intervened and broke that.

The string with issue is: `"in0_Name": "FCB_$bus % 2 FAN_$bus % 2 * 2 VOLT_V"`, which has 2 $bus in it.

When perform_scan first calls templateCharReplace for JSON pairs that do not have Name key, including `Exposes` ([code](https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/entity-manager/src/entity_manager/perform_scan.cpp?r=164af2fd1cce6c461ad43ca04e85ff0b73806ee2#489)), it handles the math with the first $bus in it. Result:

```
FCB_0 FAN_$bus % 2 * 2 VOLT_V
```

Then when it calls templateCharReplace for JSON pairs under "Exposes" ([code](https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/entity-manager/src/entity_manager/perform_scan.cpp?r=164af2fd1cce6c461ad43ca04e85ff0b73806ee2#510)), it handles the math with the second $bus in it.

But as `handleLeftOverTemplateVars` detects a leftover $bus after the first call, the second $bus in the string is removed, that's why the error log is:

```
<7> String value: `FCB_0 FAN_$bus % 2 * 2 VOLT_V`
<3> There's still template variable $bus un-replaced. Removing it from the string.
```
... and then the second call continues with no $bus left which results in a weird value on D-Bus
```
"FCB_0 FAN_ % 2 * 2 VOLT_V"
```

If `handleLeftOverTemplateVars` is removed, D-Bus will show correct string, but it will still fail if another $bus is added to the string). I don't understand why there needs to be two calls like that. At least it goes well with that specific config until `handleLeftOverTemplateVars` came into play.

When you have time, could you take a look at the issue introduced by handleLeftOverTemplateVars?

I think `handleLeftOverTemplateVars` should still detect cases where a dollar sign is left by mistake.
The regex case is quite specific, so I’d prefer to just add an exception for that.
I can't think of a scenario where a dollar sign is left at the end of a word ("Some$ random thing"). If there is, maybe it's user's intention.

> How about we check the var length here before treating it as an error?

> I think handleLeftOverTemplateVars should still detect cases where a dollar sign is left by mistake.

If there is any mistake in the config file, it is the user's fault and the user can  fix their config file.

How would we detect if the `$` is there by mistake or on purpose?

> Actually, I have the same question. If we simply skip every $, we might also miss real cases where the user accidentally left a $ by mistake.

Our plan is: If it's not intentionally configured as a variable template in the first place, whether it's user mistake or on their purpose, we should skip it from being judged.

However, I see that regex is only used in "Probe", right? And probe string should never contain a template variable because template vars are replaced by probed properties at the end, I assume?. If you want to skip regex out of this handleLeftOverTemplateVars function, I think you can just skip all JSON under "Probe" and don't touch the logic for other pairs.
If you have a better idea to fix this issue, that’d be great. This PR just proposes a simple fix because the issue was quite annoying while I was debugging EM.

) already covers this issue, we can close this PR. Thanks a lot.
I wonder why can't we just check it against strPtr->end()?

The check for strPtr->end() is to make sure we don’t dereference an invalid iterator.
The actual logic we need is to detect when the next character after $ is a quote,
so we still need to compare *firstCharIt == '\''.

I see that the capture variable logic simply uses findSpace as the end position; otherwise, it takes strPtr->end() as the end.
So in our case, it captures `$'})` instead of just `$`.

I don’t really understand why the capture logic works that way. Since this code has already been reviewed, I just excluded the regex case where the character following $ is a quote (').
That was my mistake, the regex is at the end of the probed interface, not of the JSON pair's value. Sorry for messing around.

We’ve just discovered two issues in this PR:
1.The regex anchor ($) causes a false fault log.
2.When there are two $bus variables in the same line, handleLeftOverTemplateVars may intervene and break it.

If the reviewers don’t prefer this simple fix(issue#1), this PR can be abandoned. However, I hope someone can help fix the issues introduced by PR [I4499baf3ebe9560e13932a49e324d1c8b0255623].
